title: Sovereignty spine
description: Who ruled whom, and when. Sovereignty is stored as a relation table rather than a territorial colouring, because for most of the timeline rule was graded and overlapping rather than exclusive. See docs/04-eras.md section 3.

year.description: Negative is BCE (-322 = 322 BCE). No year zero: -1 is 1 BCE, 1 is 1 CE.

id.description: POL = a polity. CUL = an archaeological culture, which is NOT a polity and cannot rule. NET = a network without evidence of centralised rule.

era.description: Era of ORIGIN, not containment. A polity may outlive or predate its era; the only invariant is that its lifespan overlaps it.

type.description: 'culture' and 'network' exist so the model can say 'nobody ruled here' without pretending a state existed.

confidence.description: How sure we are this existed as described. Climbs from ~0.45 in the Neolithic to 1.0 in the Republic; that gradient is the game's opacity setting.

core_regions.description: Coarse anchor only. Precise historical extent is a later georeferencing pour.

relation.description: One rule relation. Graded and overlapping by design: a place may simultaneously have a holder, a revenue claimant, a tributary superior and a paramount.

kind.description: Ordered roughly by how much autonomy the subordinate keeps. 'succession' means one polity replaced another rather than ruled it.
